newsitem.title: GERMANY: Henkel makes takeover bid for Loctite.
newsitem.headline: Henkel makes takeover bid for Loctite.

text.p: German consumer products group Henkel KGaA said on Monday it aimed to buy all shares it did not already own in U.S. adhesives group Loctite Corp and had offered to pay about $56 per share.
Henkel currently owns 35 percent of Loctite and expects to pay about 1.7 billion marks for the remaining 65 percent, the German company said in a mandatory statement.
In a mandatory statement, Henkel said its managing director Hans-Dietrich Winkhaus had met Loctite's president and chief executive, David Freeman, at the weekend and informed him of the bid proposal.
"Henkel offered to start talks with Loctite aimed at a swift and friendly takeover," the statement said.
Henkel said it had told Loctite that it might decide to make a public takeover bid if the talks failed to make progress or foundered.
Henkel also said that it viewed its current stake in Loctite as a permanent investment and did not aim to sell it.
Loctite's shares closed at $46 on Friday.
